title: I built a 3D pickleball learning game entirely with Claude Code. Here's how I kept it reliable.
author: Hicesias
selftext:
I wanted to see how far an AI coding agent could get building something substantially more complicated than a typical demo.

The result is Courtside Crew, a 3D pickleball game and learning tool built in Godot 4.7. It teaches the rules and strategy of pickleball through turn-based play, realistic ball physics, simulated opponents and immediate coaching feedback.

The project ran from September 12 to October 17 and grew to around 1,500 commits, 225,000 lines of game and tooling code, and 85,000 lines of tests.

The interesting part was figuring out how to keep the codebase maintainable and the results trustworthy.

A few things I put in place:

* Around 2,900 unit and integration tests across 450 files. Each test was checked against an intentionally introduced bug to make sure it could actually catch the problem it was designed for.
* Strict architectural boundaries, enforced automatically on every commit.
* Every GDScript warning treated as a compile error.
* Simulation tests comparing game behaviour against real match statistics, including checking that displayed shot probabilities match actual outcomes.
* Automated screenshot testing of every screen at 57 different device and browser sizes.
* Performance, security, build-integrity and regression checks.

The workflow was fairly simple: I'd play the game, identify something that needed fixing or improving, and turn it into an automated check. Claude would make the changes, and the checks had to pass before the work could be committed.

[This article ](https://getbetterapp.io/primer.html)goes into the details of the approach, including the parts that worked, the constraints I imposed, and some of the more unusual testing infrastructure.

Play the game in your browser, or on Mac, Windows or Linux at [itch.io.](https://courtside-crew-pickleball.itch.io/courtside-crew-pickleball)

I'd be interested to hear how others are approaching verification and architecture when using AI coding agents on projects that grow beyond prototype size. Thank you!
